description.purpose: The state surfaces of one agent's collector -- what its fan-in needs and nothing more (GH #889): `turns` holds the rows of the rounds still open and of the turns deferred behind one (session-scoped, id lexicographically time-ordered, with a `deferred` lifecycle stamp for mid-round turns - the turns-table sibling of round.fired, never content - and a `consult_id` on the rows that came in as an advisor event, which is the correlation the model is shown so it can answer the RIGHT open question), `round` is the per-turn fan-in slate that carries the assembled legs (leg-window, leg-memory, leg-brief), the tool round (assistant tool_call turns, tool results) with the fired flag both guards read, and the `depart` rows of handed-off calls (GH #728). The rows of a round fall when the round ends (OR-KX-V2); `depart` rows stay. Since collector 4.4.0 two more tables and two more columns: `session` is one row per session holding the tool scope its channel stated (`tools_allow`, `tools_deny`, GH #845) -- the one place "constant per session" is kept, read by every round the session opens; `roster` is the legend of a peer or group channel, one row per participant reference (`ref`, `name`, `identity`, `joined_at`, GH #847); and `turns.speaker`/`turns.speaker_ref` name who said a row of role `peer`. `menu` keeps each answerer's last submenu (GH #529).
description.use_when: One per collector hive. No other cell writes here; code cells own no state, so the assembly state machine keeps all of its state in this store.
description.not_in_scope: No durable memory and no conversation history: what was said is the curator's to keep (R-27-1, GH #889), and nothing here is read back beyond the round it belongs to. The channel tables are never cut with a round: `session` is replaced by delete-then-insert, and `roster` loses rows only to `roster_dedupe` and `roster_leave`. No FTS, no vectors, no canonical bindings: nothing here is retrieved by similarity.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result per op. hop.operation drives the assembly state machine, hop.rows_affected carries the RMW guard signal (a guarded update that affected 0 rows means another emission won the race and this one is terminal). hop.duration_ms is what that reply cost in milliseconds. A bundle reply (two or more tool_call turns, GH #295) stamps hop.operation 'bundle', sums hop.rows_affected over its legs and adds hop.bundle_errors: how many legs carry an error_code. That key is present on every bundle reply, 0 included, and never on a single-operation reply -- it is what an edge reads to see that one leg failed without opening the body, while hop.error_code keeps its hard meaning (the WHOLE reply is a refusal). results[]: the per-operation metadata of that same bundle reply, one entry per leg in call order -- {tool_call_id, operation, rows_affected, duration_ms} plus error_code if that one leg failed. It is a top-level body slot and not a key on the turn because a tool_result turn stays schema-pure ({origin, type, text, id}; ubf-body.json $defs/TurnObject is additionalProperties:false, so a metadata key there would dead-letter the whole reply), and tool_call_id is what ties an entry back to its turn. Like bundle_errors the slot exists only on a bundle reply -- a single-operation reply carries messages[] alone.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns with store-native args. The lane a reply belongs to is carried by context.store_origin ('collector'), the step by context.col_phase, both promoted by the edge that sent the op.
examples: {operation: insert, table: turns, row: {id, session_id, turn_id, role: 'user', content, recorded_at}} -> the turn is in the store before the round's rows are read
{operation: update, table: round, set: {fired: 1}, where: {turn_id, role: 'leg-window', fired: 0}} -> rows_affected 1 means this emission owns the fire
{operation: delete, table: round, where: {turn_id, role: {neq: 'depart'}}} -> the round ended; its rows fall, its departures stay
